name: Modern SEO - M3L3 Single Prompt Content Creation
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-22

Part of: [Modern SEO - Module 3 Core 30](lib:brain-modern-seo-module-3-core-30) | [Modern SEO Course](lib:brain-modern-seo-course) | [Learning Index](lib:brain-learning-index)

# Summary
After the gap analysis, use one detailed AI prompt (3:53) to draft the missing Core 30 pages instead of writing 15 to 25 pages by hand. Two versions: a category page prompt (broad, like Water Heater Services) and a service page prompt (specific, like tankless water heater installation). The output is about 80% of the work; human editing is the final 20%.

# Key concepts
- **Why a system:** writing 20 or 30 pages by hand takes weeks, and each needs local relevance, keywords and consistent structure. Most businesses need 15 to 25 new pages (instructor claim).
- **What the prompt produces:** title tag and meta description, heading structure with local keywords, service descriptions with geographic relevance, CTA sections, internal link suggestions.
- **Customization by service type:** emergency vs scheduled, residential vs commercial, high ticket (water heater replacement) vs routine (drain cleaning).
- **Foundational content, not final copy.** Edit for tone, local specifics and business personality.
- **Quality check 1, local:** "If the content sounds like it could work for a plumber in Miami, just as well as a plumber in Denver, have the AI regenerate it."
- **Quality check 2, accurate:** AI can invent wrong details about services, pricing or processes.
- **Why it works:** specific instructions on structure, keywords, local relevance and tone, not "write a page about drain cleaning."
- **Content is step one.** Publishing with the Core 30 internal linking and ongoing optimization builds topical authority.

# Checklist
- Right prompt for the page type.
- Title, meta, local headings, geographic relevance, CTA, link suggestions present.
- Positioning fits the service type.
- "Miami vs Denver" test passed; facts checked.
- Human edit done; published with links to category and home.

# How this applies to TAG clients
- Claude can draft Core 30 pages from the gap list; drafts go to Kim as paste-ready copy (client sites are read-only for Claude).
- The accuracy check matches Kim's no-overpromising rule: claims must be backed by the live site, the owner or Scott. Apply to every draft for [Pipeliners (Hub)](lib:brain-pipeliners-hub), [Alphalete Trenchless (Hub)](lib:brain-alphalete-trenchless-hub) and [Summit Plumbing Pros AZ (Hub)](lib:brain-summit-plumbing-pros-az-hub). See [SEO Blog Writing Standards](lib:brain-seo-blog-writing-standards).
- For Pipeliners, Scott's wording rules ("Pipeliners" only, no "pipeline" or "pipelining") are written for blogs; Kim should confirm whether they apply to Core 30 pages.
- The residential vs commercial split lines up with Alphalete's service list. Run the Miami vs Denver test especially hard on Summit AZ drafts.
- Get both prompt versions from the course page into Kim's prompt library.

# Caveats and open questions
- The prompt text is not in the video; download from the course page.
- The two-prompt process is in the paid Pro upgrade only. Per Kim's rule against paid services without approval, noted, not recommended.
- The 15 to 25 pages and 80/20 split are instructor claims.
